groups.notes:
Scope: all 14 files in src/math were read in full (1113 lines total). Kepler: no Kepler-law derivation, no equation-of-centre derivation from eccentricity, no mean-motion-from-yojana derivation and no vis-viva equation exist in src/math. The 'Vis-Viva' name (astrophysics.ts line 94) returns a constant. The nearest items are spashta.ts solveEpicycle with e = paridhi/360 left implicit (finding at line 25), and the astrophysics orbit circumferences that follow from period times equal speed (lines 21 and 27). If the owner's Kepler derivation exists, it is outside src/math; search the rest of ssea-engine.

'New relations' the file asserts as sacred or new: (a) 108 x diameter fails for five of seven grahas; (b) equal linear speed is imposed, not derived, and the orbit circumferences are period-scaled, not distances; (c) paridhi/360 used as an eccentricity-like ratio is implicit and underived; (d) R=3438 is a rounding, not a derivation. None of these is a derivation in the file.

Accuracy benchmarks: the files contain no measured accuracy claims except the header of chebyshev.ts and the 'extreme precision' comment in kerala_trig.ts, which fails against the built-ins. All numeric checks above were made by me in Python, replicating the TypeScript logic; they were not run through the engine's own test suite.

Verification limits: the folder contains no Sanskrit text, so verse numbers (SS 1.29-33, 2.34-37, 2.43-45) and the mantra strings were not checked against any source. The bhagana and epicycles values match what I recall of the standard SS lists, which is recall, not verification. The Mahayuga length of 1,577,917,500 days used in the bhagana finding is an SS value not in this folder. Modern sidereal periods and distances (Sun 365.256363 d, Moon 27.321661 d, Mars 686.980 d, Mercury 87.9691 d, Jupiter 4332.589 d, Venus 224.7008 d, Saturn 10759.22 d; Moon 384,400 km, Sun 1.496e8 km) are recalled standard values.

Bugs confirmed by reading and replication: aryabhata NaN at 90 and 270 degrees; astrophysics key mismatch (SURYA, SUKRA) silently returning 0 or throwing; pingala getNashtam accepting out-of-range index; samudra churn without dt; mahabharata time-dilation domain; ramayana divide by zero at resolveFactor 0; spashta sign comments contradict the code; chebyshev dead branch at line 77.

SCOPE. Read in full: src/surya.ts (218 lines), src/candra.ts (576), src/planet-helpers.ts (445), src/core/ahargana.ts (18), src/core/vedic_ephemeris.ts (44). src/core has no other .ts files (core/README.md exists and was not read; it is not .ts). DERIVATIONS. None of Kepler's laws; no equation-of-centre derivation from first principles; no manda-phala ↔ eccentricity derivation; no mean motion from yojana orbits; no 108 × diameter or equal-linear-speed relation in these files. The Kepler solve is standard Newton. The equation-of-centre series is a standard textbook expansion stated without derivation. The manda identity r = epicycle-peripheri/360 is asserted, and the file itself says the Sun's 14° is not the true eccentricity (surya L36-37). The in-file derivations are the sign algebra (candra L62-67, L72-75), the Ujjain 166′ arithmetic (candra L93), and the u = λ − Ω and sin β construction (planet-helpers L349-356, L410-414). VERSE QUOTATIONS. No Sanskrit verse text anywhere in scope. Only Karaṇa-kutūhala sub-term names (candra L55, L59, L70) and verse numbers IV.7-12.

FITTED VALUES. KEPLER_COEFFS (planet-helpers L25-54; no source named); one dṛk epoch phase per planet (L159-161); the 21-term dṛk-śeṣa tail (candra L555-558; file says fitted, held-out validated).

groups.notes:
Coverage: I read grahana.ts (389 lines), udaya.ts (595), lagna.ts (350) and aberration.ts (100) in full. For grahana-catalog.ts I read the header, the first and last catalog blocks, grepped all section headers and per-year counts, and checked the 1920-1949 gap and the 2020-2030 row count. I did not read every catalog row. I did not use the network, so NASA values are not checked against the source.

Kepler and derivation search: I found no derivation of Kepler's laws, no equation-of-centre derivation, no manda-phala-to-eccentricity relation, no mean motions from yojana orbits, no "108 × diameter" relation, and no "equal linear speeds" claim in these five files. The only "derivation" statements are the S-S/Bhāskara attributions (asserted) and the small arithmetic checks listed above. The kepler/manda/yojana material, if it exists, must be in another file of the engine.

Sanskrit verse: the BhP 3.11.5 quotation (aberration.ts lines 22-23) was not checked against a critical edition. The gloss at line 25 is contradicted by the verse's content as the file reproduces it (length measures). The S-S verse numbers (III.17-21, III.42-50, IV.6, IV.7, IV.10, V.4, V.7, V.13, II.66) appear only as citations; none is quoted in these files, so none is text-verified here.

Catalog structure: 554 rows of {kind, year, month, day, hourUT, typeCode, magnitude}. Years 1920-1949 have zero rows. Blocks from 2031 onward are labelled "forward projection - Saros recurrence" in comments, while the header calls all rows NASA canon data.

Engine candidates (ranked by expected gain): (1) udaya EoT with mean sun instead of true longitude (up to about 7 min), (2) planetary light-time for outer planets (several arcsec), (3) geometric eclipse detector in grahana, (4) fill the catalog gap 1920-1949 and separate projected from NASA rows, (5) IAU 2006 obliquity in lagna (small), (6) e-term in aberration (about 0.34 arcsec).

Unverified numbers I flagged but did not confirm: the classical S-S ayanamsa "~77°" (udaya.ts:237), the S-S obliquity "24°" used in finding udaya.ts:41, and the eclipse-limit attribution to S-S V.13. Please check those against the texts before relying on them.

Scope: 18 files (src/os 12, src/predictive 5, src/ui 1), all read in full with line numbers. Total about 1643 lines.

Your requested items, checked against these files:
- Kepler's laws or a Kepler derivation: NONE in scope.
- Equation of centre or manda-phala vs eccentricity: NONE in scope. The nearest is motion.ts (sighra kendra = sighrocca - madhyama, retrograde bands), which is a planetary-sighra relation, not an eccentricity derivation.
- Mean motions from yojana orbits: NONE in scope.
- 108 x diameter or equal linear speeds: NONE in scope. The 108 relations are arithmetic only: 27x4=108 (master-matrix.ts:16, sphota.ts:88), 144=12x12, 3888=144x27, 104976=3888x27, 972=104976/108. The file's own 972 label cites an external 'system document' not in this tree (master-matrix.ts:62).
- Fitted (JPL/Drik) values: NONE in scope.
- Benchmarks or accuracy claims: NONE with a measured reference. motion.ts:17 calls its bands 'approximate'. dasha.ts and btr_module.ts make no accuracy claim.
- Verse quotations with a number: panini.ts only (Ashtadhyayi 1.1.9, 6.1.77, 6.1.87, 6.1.88, 6.1.101, 8.2.1, 8.2.39). These are correct sutra numbers and sutra text as I know them, but I did not check them against an external source. The Shiva-sutra array (57 entries) matches the 14 standard sutras. The 108-entry Avakahada syllable table is traditional and uncited.

Verified in this run (by probe or count):
- sphota.ts AVAKAHADA_CHAKRA has 108 entries (grep count).
- Shiva-sutra array has 57 entries (sum of the 14 standard sutra lengths).
- The Yan glide map gives u -> y, not v (probe on a transcription of the Sthana matrix and findClosestPhoneme; enum could not be run directly, since no TypeScript runner is in the repo).
- Kali half-life from 0.000108 is 6418.0 days (my computation).
- Master-matrix integer chain: 144*27=3888, 3888*27=104976, 104976/108=972.

Most important defects for the receiving engine, in priority order:
1. panini.ts:145 Yan sandhi maps u to y (should be v). Also ri/lri guna and phoneme-vs-character handling (lines 128, 150).
2. varga.ts:49-50 D27 is a mod-12 sign index, not the 1-27 nakshatramsha, and its element comments do not match the code. D60 has no odd/even split while D7 and D10 do.
3. dasha.ts uses the mean Moon (btr_module.ts:78) while the file comment claims full Surya Siddhanta mechanics. A sphuta-Moon option is the main accuracy candidate here.
4. brahmand_os.ts:59 logs that Kali and Brahmastra are triggered, but triggerLaya never calls them.
5. motion.ts retrograde bands are unsourced approximations, and all five are symmetric about 180 by construction.

Provenance caution: almost all numeric content in these files is owner-framework or unsourced. The only modern-standard constants are the Stefan-Boltzmann sigma (mahavidya.ts:110), Gregorian year 365.2425 (dasha.ts:25), 1440 min/day (btr_module.ts:122), and the 360/27 nakshatra arithmetic (nakshatra.ts:28).

findings.summary: Rahu retrograde mean daily motion. The file names no source. groups.notes:
Scope: 27 root files matching the patterns (calculate_laksha, compare_*, generate_my_kundali, run_*, strict_btr, all test-*.ts) plus 8 files in scratch/ = 35 files, all read in full. Not read (out of scope): ssea_core.ts, ssea_absolute.ts, src/**, package files.

Kepler and derivations: no derivation of Kepler's laws, the equation of centre, the manda-phala relation to eccentricity, or mean motions from yojana orbits exists in scope. The Kepler code (scratch/mangal-kundali.ts 24-34, also prithvi-kundali.ts and test-mangal-kendra.ts) is a numerical Newton solve plus standard conic relations, asserted not derived. test-spashta.ts calls getMandaPhala from src/, which is out of scope. The one real derivation in scope is test-mangal-kendra-mean.ts lines 45-47 (Sun-from-Mars rate identity). The only "sacred" relation is 108 x diameter (test-astrophysics.ts:18); the file gives no derivation for it. No equal-linear-speed relation appears in scope.

Verse quotations: none in scope. Grep found no verse numbers, sloka or sutra numbers, and no BPHS chapter. Sources are named only by text or tradition (Surya Siddhanta, BPHS, Ashtadhyayi by incipit, Aryabhata, Ramayana, Nilakantha) without verse references.

Constants with text attribution: none carry a verse number. Chebyshev coefficients in test-chebyshev.ts are modern Bessel values (c_n = 2 I_n(1)), not a Siddhanta source. Lahiri ayanamsa (used in several scratch and test files) is a 20th-century convention, and prithvi-kundali-bharat.ts line 49 labels the same output PURE Surya Siddhanta, which is a contradiction in the owner's labelling.

Benchmarks: test-moon-deg.ts line 123 (5 arcsec max error against the owner's own series) is the only accuracy criterion. Most test files print values with no expected results and no assertions (test-chebyshev, test-panini, test-spashta, test-bphs, test-predictive, test-epics-integration, test-mangal-kendra). They are demonstrations, not regression tests.

Inconsistencies found: (1) BirthTimeRectifier is called with two incompatible signatures and two result-field casings across files. (2) Laksha base time appears as 16:03, 16:06, 16:07:30, 16:09, and 16:10 across files. (3) J2000 is written as 2451545.5 in test-predictive and test-vedic, and as 2451545.0 in test-moon-deg and fit-chebyshev. (4) test-shadbala JD label is half a day off. (5) strict_btr printed bound 04:05-04:10 PM does not match its comment 16:04-16:10. (6) generate_my_kundali silently defaults a missing graha to 0.

Rahu constant check: 0.052976 deg/day corresponds to about 232,199 revolutions per 1,577,917,500-day mahayuga (my arithmetic). I believe the Surya Siddhanta count is 232,226 (about 0.0529821 deg/day). This is unverified; the owner should check the verse before relying on either number.

Personal data: the scope names real people and dated life events (2017-2024). I have not repeated those dates in the findings beyond the birth times needed to show the inconsistency.
